clue.text: At sea David's got nausea — it's not helping at all!

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and all over the place, so the following letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Seasick David is no use to anyone on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' looks like scene-setting for the nausea, but it signals that DAVIDS GOT NAUSEA is rearranged; the possessive apostrophe is ignored and 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unfavourable or detrimental gives no help at all.

clue.text: And then — devil starts heat torture?

definitions.text: And then — devil starts heat torture?

indicators.note: starts tells us to take only the opening letter of the word devil
to torture is to twist and wrench, so the letters of heat are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A grim question about what follows the end of life: the devil sets about tormenting you with heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torture' twists the letters of 'heat' after the devil's first letter. Read whole, the clue asks what comes before hellfire, which is the definition; 'And then' belongs to that reading.
explanation.definitionFit: In the traditional picture of hell, the devil's fiery torments begin only once life has ended.

clue.text: Stay to have something to eat and drink

parts.note: to sup is to take supper, an evening meal
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: An invitation to linger over food and a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay' looks like a verb inviting you to remain, but it is a noun: a prop or brace.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a prop or brace, something that holds another thing up.

clue.text: Acting stupidly, is told off

indicators.note: off here means wrong or out of order, so the letters of told are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone behaving like an idiot gets a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' reads as part of 'told off' (scolded) but is the anagram signal on TOLD. The definition is loose: it describes the one acting stupidly, and 'is' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool or blockhead is a person given to stupid behaviour.

clue.text: Girl takes a pudding — it's just greed

parts.note: Ava is a girl's name
rice pudding, often just called rice

explanation.surface: A girl helps herself to dessert out of sheer gluttony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes a' is link material joining the girl to the pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Grasping greed for wealth is the sin of covetousness.

clue.text: Present in metal container is in that place

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a tin is a metal can
present, as in here rather than absent

explanation.surface: A gift has been packed inside a tin box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift but means 'here', in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: An old formal adverb meaning within that thing or location.

clue.text: Prime material for the plot

parts.note: the plot is the 1605 conspiracy to blow up Parliament, and this explosive was its key material; 'prime' also hints at priming a charge

explanation.surface: A novelist hunts for the best ideas for a storyline.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gunpowder Plot, Guy Fawkes's 1605 attempt to blow up the Houses of Parliament, is remembered in Britain every 5 November.
explanation.definitionFit: The black explosive powder was the material Guy Fawkes's conspirators stockpiled under Parliament.

clue.text: Once the top is off tilts and removes the content

indicators.note: with the top off, the first letter of the word is lost

parts.note: to tilt is to joust, charging with a lance

explanation.surface: Someone tips a container to empty out what is inside once the lid is off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tilts' looks like tipping a vessel but is the knightly sense; JOUSTS loses its first letter J. 'Once' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject or expel is to turn out whoever or whatever occupies a place.

clue.text: Focus attention on vessel student brought into view

indicators.note: brought into tells us the first pieces go inside the word for view

parts.note: a sight is a view
a pot is a vessel
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student discovers a pot and puts it on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought into' puts the vessel and the student inside the view. L stands for learner, from the L-plates British learner drivers display.
explanation.definitionFit: To highlight something is to direct people's attention to it, like a stage lamp on a performer.

clue.text: Before noon, swig at a flask

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, is before noon
a pull is a swig from a bottle

explanation.surface: Someone takes a morning drink from a flask.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A small two-handled vessel for oil or wine, as used in Roman times and in church ritual.

clue.text: This italian boy found bird's egg on square

indicators.note: on means placed after, the egg following the square in an across answer

parts.note: an erne is a sea eagle, so bird's gives erne plus S
T, from a T-square, the drawing tool
O, shaped like an egg

explanation.surface: An Italian lad discovers a bird's egg in a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: As held, 'in' gives no order that builds the answer; read as 'on', O follows ERNES and T.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian masculine given name, the counterpart of Ernest.

clue.text: Eye-catching gadget

parts.note: in a ...-and-eye fastening, the little curved metal piece literally catches the eye

explanation.surface: A striking new device draws attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eye-catching' seems to mean striking but is literal: the gadget that catches the eye of a fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: On clothing, a curved metal fastener engages a small loop called an eye.

clue.text: Conclusive reformulation of magisterial position

indicators.note: a reformulation reworks something, so the letters of conclusive are rearranged

explanation.surface: A decisive rewording of a judge's stance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conclusive' is all the fodder; 'reformulation of' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy consul holds a diplomatic office representing a state abroad, a post of official authority.

clue.text: Banker bringing in wine relaxed regulations

indicators.note: bringing in tells us the river's letters wrap round the wine

parts.note: a banker is a thing with banks, a river; the Dee is a British river
tent is a deep red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: A banker with wine in hand celebrates looser rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' is the crossword joke for a river (it has banks): the Dee. TENT, an old name for Spanish red wine, goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An easing of tension between rival nations, as in the Cold War thaw.

clue.text: Seed spilling out from box into soil

indicators.note: seed spilling out is scattered, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: a crate is a box

explanation.surface: A gardener tips seed from a box into the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soil' looks like earth in this garden scene but is a verb meaning defile. DESE is SEED rearranged; 'from' and 'into' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To profane or defile something sacred is to sully it.

clue.text: Snooper on the prowl in outskirts of Nuneaton? He's of no significance

indicators.note: in tells us the scrambled letters go between the outer ones
outskirts are the edges of a town, so take the first and last letters of Nuneaton
prowling around, the letters of snooper roam into a new order

explanation.surface: A nosy parker prowls the edge of a Midlands town.
explanation.walkthrough: Nuneaton is a town in Warwickshire, England; its outskirts give N and N, around NOPERSO, the anagram of SNOOPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone treated as nonexistent or unimportant, whose existence is ignored.

clue.text: Agreeably sleepy?

explanation.surface: Pleasantly drowsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dipping the head signals assent, and a drowsy person's head droops the same way.

clue.text: I'm working on repairs for the showmen

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

indicators.note: working on something reshapes it, so the letters of repairs are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone busy fixing things for the entertainers.
explanation.walkthrough: PRESARI is REPAIRS rearranged, signalled by 'working'; 'on' and 'for' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatrical managers or promoters who stage shows, the plural of an Italian loanword.

clue.text: Those under the vehicle don't hold water

explanation.surface: Something beneath a car is leaky.
explanation.walkthrough: A ship's timber springs when it cracks and lets water in.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's suspension uses coiled or leaf steel coils beneath the body; a vessel that leaks has sprung open.

clue.text: A swell a construction like, this should contain

definitions.text: A swell a construction like, this should contain

indicators.note: a construction is something built up, so the letters are assembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A big wave is the very thing such a structure is built to hold back.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is A SWELL A, rearranged as signalled by 'construction'; read whole, a coastal barrier like this should hold back a swell.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal barrier is built to keep heavy waves off the land.

clue.text: Wall is a theatrical role with mimic in it

indicators.note: with the mimic in it says one piece goes inside the role

parts.note: a part is an actor's role
to ape is to mimic

explanation.surface: An actor's part includes a bit of mimicry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is a' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A low protective barrier along a roof, bridge or balcony edge.

clue.text: Bundle of cards collected over a considerable time

parts.note: a pack of cards
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: A bundle of cards gathered over a long period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collected over' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A parcel is a wrapped bundle sent or carried.

clue.text: Vehicle for transferring land

explanation.surface: A means of moving property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A carriage or other means of transport; and in law, the deed transferring property title.

clue.text: The occasion — midmorning at some time in the past

parts.note: the middle letter of the word morning

parts.words: at some time in the past
parts.note: once means formerly

explanation.surface: A special event happened one morning long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the nonce' means for the present occasion. 'midmorning' gives the middle letter of MORNING.
explanation.definitionFit: A word surviving in the phrase 'for the time being', meaning for this particular purpose.

clue.text: Pool part of summer earnings

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone pools a portion of their holiday wages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pool' looks like a verb about money; it is a small lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A small lake or pond, mostly in English place names.

clue.text: Whipped, the top skimmed off and then consumed.

indicators.note: skimming off the top removes the first letter

parts.note: whipped, as cream is, means beaten

explanation.surface: Cream whipped, skimmed and then eaten up.
explanation.walkthrough: BEATEN loses its first letter B; 'and then' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has been swallowed or devoured.

clue.text: Not a close ring for gamblers

parts.note: not near is distant
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Gamblers huddled in a loose ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a loose pointer to the game itself: a card game played for bets.
explanation.definitionFit: An old banking card game, popular in Wild West saloons for wagering.

clue.text: One won't remember having it

parts.note: the joke is that the condition itself prevents you recalling having it

explanation.surface: A forgotten thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Memory loss means the sufferer cannot recall things, possibly including the loss.

clue.text: It's hard for first mate to can easily

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'It's hard for first mate to can easily (7)'. ADAM (first mate, Eve's) is clear, but 'to can easily' gives no ANT; the text seems garbled in OCR and no source found.
annotationWithheld.clue: It's hard for first mate to can easily

clue.text: I note ardent love changing yet unchanging

definitions.text: I note ardent love changing yet unchanging

indicators.note: changing means altering, so the letters of the preceding words are shuffled

explanation.surface: A paradox: affection rearranged, yet constant.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder I NOTE ARDENT LOVE rearranges to the answer; 'yet unchanging' makes the joke: the letters change, the love does not.
explanation.definitionFit: Undying, everlasting affection is a love that never alters.
